title: Trump Signs Executive Order Creating US Space Academy at Houston Stop
detail: President Trump signed an executive order on Friday, August 28, 2026, at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, establishing the nation's first U.S. Space Academy — a new federal institution to train personnel for the Space Force, NASA, and the civilian space industry. The order creates a Presidential Commission on the U.S. Space Academy chaired by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, and science advisor Michael Kratsios also involved; the commission has 120 days to deliver a report on governance, curriculum, and site selection, with Trump saying a location would be chosen 'very shortly.' The signing came during a Houston stop in which Trump also awarded medals to the Artemis II crew.

media.caption: Trump signs an executive order establishing the US Space Academy at NASA's Johnson Space Center

title: Judge Rejects Trump's Third Attempt to Move Hush Money Case to Federal Court
detail: US District Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein on Friday, August 28, 2026 rejected President Trump's third attempt to move his New York hush money conviction from state to federal court, where Trump's legal team hoped to invoke broader presidential immunity following a Supreme Court immunity ruling to have the conviction tossed. Hellerstein, who has now blocked the removal bid three times, wrote that 'the grounds for a second removal cited by Defendant, Donald J. Trump, are neither new nor legally sufficient' and that Trump 'failed to show good cause and diligence.' Trump was convicted in 2024 on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records tied to a $130,000 hush payment to Stephanie Clifford (Stormy Daniels).

media.caption: A federal judge rejects Trump's third bid to move his hush money case to federal court
